claim: As of April 30, 2025, every io2 volume, new or previously created, is an io2 Block Express volume; before, an io2 volume that did not run on Block Express ranged from 4 GiB to 16 TiB, with up to 64,000 IOPS per volume and a maximum IOPS-to-GiB ratio of 500:1.

values.spoken: up to sixty-four thousand IOPS per volume

evidence.quote: As of **April 30, 2025**, all new and previously created `io2` volumes are `io2` Block Express volumes.
evidence.title: Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes

evidence.quote: Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes can range in size from 4 GiB to 16 TiB, and you can provision from 100 IOPS up to 64,000 IOPS per volume.
The maximum ratio of provisioned IOPS to requested volume size (in GiB) is 50:1 for `io1` volumes, and 500:1 for `io2` volumes.
Provisioned IOPS SSD `io1` and `io2` volumes are available for all Amazon EC2 instance types.

changed.was: io2 volumes not on Block Express: 4 GiB to 16 TiB, up to 64,000 IOPS per volume, IOPS-to-GiB ratio 500:1

note: fr-0071 (requests-22): the old io2 limits come from the AWS whitepaper 'Optimizing PostgreSQL running on Amazon EC2 using Amazon EBS' (page written when only io2 volumes on listed Nitro instance families ran on Block Express; its next paragraph gives io2 Block Express 256,000 IOPS and 1,000:1). The What's New posts of 2020-08, 2020-12 and 2023-11-21 are blocked by robots.txt. FRESHNESS dated steps 2023-11-21 (all new io2 on Nitro) and 2025-07-22 (Regions); the provisioned-iops page gives April 30, 2025 for all io2 volumes.
